About Us

Nexfibre is a next generation fibre broadband company, formed in December 2022 as a joint venture between InfraVia Capital Partners, Liberty Global and Telefónica. We are on a mission to deliver high-speed broadband to up to 7 million homes across the UK over the next 4 years. We are backed by a £4.5 billion investment by our investors and banks.

Working closely with our commercial partner Virgin Media O2, we will create the only national scale fibre to the home network to compete with BT Openreach. We are supporting the Government’s ambition to tackle digital exclusion, deliver nationwide ultrafast broadband rollout by 2030 and level up disconnected communities by investing in the areas we’re building in and acting as a net-contributor.

Nexfibre is a small, growing and dynamic organization. We look to attract high performing, energetic and entrepreneurial team members with a growth mindset.

Job Purpose

The Telecoms Security Compliance Analyst will support the delivery, coordination, and tracking of security governance, compliance, policy implementation and training activities across nexfibre, including tracking obligations relating to the Telecommunications (Security) Act and relevant regulatory requirements.

This role is primarily operational and administrative in nature, helping maintain governance processes, evidence tracking, reporting cadence and awareness activities.

Principle Responsibilities Of The Role Will Be

Maintain and update compliance trackers, action logs, risk registers and evidence repositories.
Support monitoring of obligations related to the Telecommunications (Security) Act and associated security frameworks.
Assist in preparing governance updates, dashboards, metrics, and reporting packs for internal stakeholders.
Coordinate collection of evidence for audits, assurance reviews and regulatory requests, including s135 requests from Ofcom.
Ensure all supporting compliance documentation such as the Information Security Compliance Toolkit including Asset Register, Business Impact Assessment, Risk Treatment Plan are kept up to date.
Assist in the rollout and maintenance of security policies, standards, procedures and guidance documents.
Track policy compliance, review cycles and feedback collection and assist with training materials and internal guidance.

Key Accountabilities

Assist the Regulatory and Security Lead in managing and obtaining information to ensure risk and governance processes are up to date and managed as required.
Support Regulatory and Security Lead by maintaining and updating records.

Knowledge & Experience

Strong organizational and administrative skills.
Interest in cybersecurity, governance, risk and compliance.
Working knowledge of the Telecoms Security Act.
Exposure to compliance frameworks such as ISO 27001, NIST, Cyber Essentials.
Experience of analyzing, reporting and presenting data in multiple ways.
Experience supporting governance, audit or compliance activities.
Experience coordinating training and awareness initiatives.
Understanding of risk management, IT and networking principles.
Ideally educated to degree level and holding a professional Information Security qualification such as CISSP or CISM.

Benefits

Competitive salary and bonus scheme
25 days’ annual leave, plus the usual 8 UK Bank Holidays
Bupa private healthcare coverage
Access to wellbeing and mental health benefits such as the WeCare app, critical illness cover, dental & optical insurance
Pension contribution matched up to 10%
Access to our car benefit scheme via Tusker and our Cycle to Work scheme
Virgin Media / O2 discounts and offers

LOCATION

We are based in Paddington. The position is full time, hybrid with a minimum 3 days based in the office. Nexfibre is an equal opportunity employer. We embrace diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for our people.

We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.

jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Supply Planning Analyst will assist the supply planning function for RealTruck. The primary purpose of this role will be to develop, deploy, implement, and lead best-in-class Supply Planning and Inventory Management processes, including network wide capacity management, production scheduling, and inventory management.

Core Functions

Support the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of Supply Planning processes and procedures within the RealTruck S&OP process.
Develop and maintain rough-cut capacity planning and network capacity analyses at the value stream, plant, and subgroup levels to identify constraints, capacity gaps, and opportunities to align supply with demand.
Analyze and refresh, on an as needed basis, manufacturing value streams and manufacturing flow based on demand characteristics.
Support the production planning and scheduling process by analyzing production requirements, inventory positions, capacity constraints, and demand priorities. Participate in recurring production and supply planning reviews, highlighting risks, deviations from plan, and potential solutions.
Develop, maintain, and analyze Supply Chain dashboards and key performance indicators (KPIs), including Schedule Adherence/Attainment, On-Time Delivery (OTD), Fill Rate, inventory levels, days of supply, and other relevant planning metrics.
Analyze planning rates and assumptions, including hours per unit (HPU), production rates, efficiencies, and demonstrated versus planned capacity, and recommend updates where appropriate.
Develop and maintain statistical inventory models (model stock) to set target finish good and raw material inventory levels.
Support the development and maintenance of finished goods and component inventory policies, including safety stock levels, stocking strategies, replenishment parameters, economic order quantities, and Kanban sizing.
Partner with cross-functional teams to investigate supply, inventory, and capacity issues and provide data-driven recommendations to support business decisions.

Qualifications & Requirements

Education and Experience

Bachelor’s Degree in Supply Chain, Operations Management, Finance, Economics, or a similarly analytical discipline is required.
2-5+ years of related experience in Supply Chain or Operational Finance required.
Expertise in Demand Planning/Supply Planning.

Required Licenses

None.

Skills, Abilities, And Knowledge

Versed with best-in-class ERP/MRP systems (use, calibration, setting of parameters) and other useful platforms (Excel, Access).
Ability to effectively present information to top management.
Ability to analyze and communicate numerical data utilizing analysis capabilities.
Ability to work cross-functionally with manufacturing, sales and finance.

Occasional travel may be required.

– Approaches others in a tactful manner; Reacts well under pressure; Treats others with respect and consideration regardless of their status or position; Accepts responsibility for own actions; Follows through on commitments.
– Balances team and individual responsibilities; Exhibits objectivity and openness to other views; Gives and welcomes feedback; Contributes to building a positive team spirit; Puts success of team above own interests; Supports everyone’s efforts to succeed.
– Speaks clearly and persuasively in positive or negative situations; listens and gets clarification; Responds well to questions; Demonstrates group presentation skills; Participates in meetings.
– Writes clearly and informatively; Edits work for spelling and grammar; Varies writing style to meet needs; Presents numerical data effectively; Able to read and interpret written information.

Supervisor Responsibilities

Individual Contributor

Physical Requirements

This position is subject to Sedentary Work: Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally and/or a negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise move objects. Sedentary work involved sitting most of the time. Walking and standing are required only occasionally.

Physical Activities

Visual Acuity

The worker is required to have close visual acuity to perform an activity such as preparing and analyzing data and figures; transcribing; viewing a computer terminal; expansive reading; visual inspection involving small defects, small parts and/or operation of machines (including inspection); using measurement devices; and/or assembly of fabrication of parts at distances close to the eyes.

Working Conditions

Enjoy great benefits like medical, dental, and vision coverage, company-paid life insurance and disability, and a 401(k) with company match (eligible the first of the month after you start). TL;DR

This is a senior hybrid role, half building the scaled programs engine, half account ownership. You'll own a cohort of scaled customers directly, running their onboarding, driving adoption, and retaining them, while designing the scaled enablement programs, curricula, webinars, onboarding journeys, and lifecycle communications, that teach an entire customer base how to build with Lovable.

Your book of accounts is a test bed and a live classroom. What you prove there becomes the playbook for the whole CS organization. This role suits a past CSM ready to multiply their impact through scaled education, content, and automation, owning revenue outcomes like a CSM while building like a program leader.

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we're just getting started.

We're building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME's 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe's fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

What You'll Do

Scaled programs (~50%)

Own post-purchase lifecycle communications and customer education across every channel and segment: email, in-app guides, Slack, release comms, and re-engagement plays
Architect Lovable's customer education academy, defining learning paths, designing the curricula and content (courses, video, labs, certification-ready material), and owning the roadmap from first course to a full academy
Build and host live education, including onboarding sessions, workshops, and feature deep-dives, turning recordings into an on-demand library
Design the digital onboarding journey for scaled customers, with sequenced comms, in-app guidance, and self-serve resources anchored to the learning paths
Package content into repeatable formats CSMs can deliver in their own accounts
Instrument everything to tie education and program performance to retention

Customer ownership (~50%)

Own a book of ~100s scaled-segment accounts end to end: run a disciplined renewal motion and manage risk early through direct engagement and automated plays, monitoring account health along the way, with most accounts self-served through your programs and your time reserved for moments of risk and opportunity
Guide customers from first project to load-bearing app, helping admins deploy the platform well and helping builders ship applications their teams depend on

Surface product blockers, expansion signals, and success stories to Product, Sales, and Marketing, capturing the voice of the customer

How We'll Measure Success

Scaled CS runs on the same core metrics as the rest of the team, no separate scoreboard.

Gross retention (DRR/GRR) on your book, the north star for the segment
Net active builders and net load-bearing apps, the impact of your programs across all accounts
Education metrics: learning-path completion, live session engagement, and time-to-first-value for educated vs. non-educated cohorts
Program metrics: onboarding completion, comms performance, and re-engagement conversion
Leverage metrics: motions from your book that graduate to team-wide adoption

6-8+ years in Scaled Success, customer success, customer education, or post-sales roles, with direct ownership of renewals and a track record of strong retention
Deep experience designing and delivering one-to-many programs at scale: curricula, learning paths or academies, webinars, digital onboarding, lifecycle email, or community, spanning both instructor-led and self-serve formats
A builder's instinct: comfortable prototyping with modern tools including Lovable itself, automating your own workflows, and using AI to extend your reach
Strong written and presentation skills, sharp enough to write an email sequence that converts and hold a room of 200 customers
Data fluency: you form hypotheses, instrument the programs to test them, and let results decide what scales
Comfort with ambiguity and a bias to ship, this segment is being built and you'll help define how it works
Bonus: experience in a consumption/credit-based pricing model, PLG-to-enterprise motion, or developer/builder-adjacent products

Position Summary

The Inventory Planning Analyst will support the inventory planning and optimization function for RealTruck. The primary purpose of this role is to analyze inventory requirements, develop and maintain inventory policies, and support strategies that balance product availability, customer service, and working capital objectives. This role will partner cross-functionally with Supply Planning, Demand Planning, Operations, Procurement, and other business functions to improve inventory health across the network.

Core Functions

Support the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of Inventory Planning processes and procedures within the RealTruck S&OP process.
Analyze inventory levels across plants, distribution centers, and product groups to identify shortages, excess and obsolete inventory, and opportunities to improve inventory health and working capital.
Conduct regular reviews of inventory targets and planning parameters to ensure inventory policies remain aligned with changes in demand, lead times, supply performance, product lifecycle, and corporate inventory objectives.
Support the development and maintenance of inventory policies, including safety stock levels, stocking strategies, replenishment parameters, minimum and maximum inventory levels, economic order quantities, and Kanban sizing.
Develop, maintain, and analyze inventory dashboards and key performance indicators (KPIs), including inventory value, days of supply, inventory turns, fill rate, service level, excess and obsolete inventory, and inventory performance versus target.
Analyze inventory positioning across the distribution and manufacturing network and provide recommendations to improve product availability, reduce excess inventory, and optimize inventory deployment.
Analyze historical demand, forecast performance, lead times, order quantities, and inventory consumption patterns to identify opportunities to improve inventory planning parameters and stocking strategies.
Support continuous improvement initiatives focused on inventory optimization, working capital reduction, service-level improvement, and increased visibility into inventory performance across the network.

Position Summary

The Inventory Planning Analyst will support the inventory planning and optimization function for RealTruck. The primary purpose of this role is to analyze inventory requirements, develop and maintain inventory policies, and support strategies that balance product availability, customer service, and working capital objectives. This role will partner cross-functionally with Supply Planning, Demand Planning, Operations, Procurement, and other business functions to improve inventory health across the network.

Core Functions

Support the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of Inventory Planning processes and procedures within the RealTruck S&OP process.
Analyze inventory levels across plants, distribution centers, and product groups to identify shortages, excess and obsolete inventory, and opportunities to improve inventory health and working capital.
Conduct regular reviews of inventory targets and planning parameters to ensure inventory policies remain aligned with changes in demand, lead times, supply performance, product lifecycle, and corporate inventory objectives.
Support the development and maintenance of inventory policies, including safety stock levels, stocking strategies, replenishment parameters, minimum and maximum inventory levels, economic order quantities, and Kanban sizing.
Develop, maintain, and analyze inventory dashboards and key performance indicators (KPIs), including inventory value, days of supply, inventory turns, fill rate, service level, excess and obsolete inventory, and inventory performance versus target.
Analyze inventory positioning across the distribution and manufacturing network and provide recommendations to improve product availability, reduce excess inventory, and optimize inventory deployment.
Analyze historical demand, forecast performance, lead times, order quantities, and inventory consumption patterns to identify opportunities to improve inventory planning parameters and stocking strategies.
Support continuous improvement initiatives focused on inventory optimization, working capital reduction, service-level improvement, and increased visibility into inventory performance across the network.
Identify slow-moving and excess inventory and partner with cross-functional teams to develop mitigation strategies, including inventory rebalancing, consumption plans, stocking policy changes, and other corrective actions.

Qualifications & Requirements

Education and Experience

Bachelor’s Degree in Supply Chain, Operations Management, Finance, Economics, or a similarly analytical discipline is required.
2-5+ years of related experience in Supply Chain or Operational Finance required.
Expertise in Demand Planning/Supply Planning/Inventory Management.

Versed with best-in-class ERP/MRP systems (use, calibration, setting of parameters) and other useful platforms (Excel, Access).
Ability to effectively present information to top management.

Ability to work cross-functionally with manufacturing, sales and finance.
